intro: I’m Abinav, a Data Engineer with 3 years of professional experience at Virtusa, working on BMO’s financial data platform. I genuinely enjoy building things, working with data, and getting to the bottom of why things break 😅. I’d absolutely love to discuss what I can bring to your team and how I could contribute to Walmart as a whole.
whyCompany: Walmart’s data engineering roles connect large-scale pipelines to analytical datasets that business teams can trust. Their recurring focus on SQL, cloud warehouses, data quality, performance and distributed data processing matches the work I do in financial data engineering: delivering reporting data, managing dependencies and keeping batch workflows dependable.

The opportunity to contribute to those problems at Walmart’s scale is what draws me here. I bring production Python, SQL, PySpark, Airflow and AWS experience, alongside hands-on Snowflake and dbt work in my personal Retail Sales Lakehouse. That gives me a concrete foundation for contributing to batch processing and analytical datasets while continuing to deepen my Spark expertise.

canHelp.title: Scalable batch pipelines
canHelp.body: Walmart’s pipeline roles need repeatable ingestion and dependable downstream delivery. At Virtusa for BMO, I built and maintained Python, SQL and PySpark ETL using Glue, S3 and Airflow, including incremental loads and dependencies across 150+ daily production runs. I would bring that experience to batch workflows serving analytical datasets.

canHelp.title: PySpark processing · Production + personal project
canHelp.body: PySpark is part of my hands-on data engineering experience at BMO, where I have worked with PySpark alongside Python, SQL and AWS-based ETL workflows in an enterprise financial data environment. I have also gone deeper independently through my Retail Sales Lakehouse, where I used PySpark for window-based deduplication, schema enforcement, enrichment and row-level rejects, with partitioned Parquet and idempotent batch processing.

canHelp.title: Data quality and production recovery
canHelp.body: Reliable datasets require checks and a clear recovery path. My automated validation for schema mismatches, date inconsistencies, missing columns and duplicates reduced recurring issues by 25%. I also use CloudWatch, investigate upstream and Glue/Redshift failures, and execute controlled reruns; since June 2026, I’ve held offshore L3 support ownership.

canHelp.title: Warehouse performance and useful models
canHelp.body: Walmart’s warehouse roles emphasize efficient queries and analytics-ready models. My layered Redshift raw-to-reporting models delivered 40% faster queries, and tuned COPY loads were 3× faster than row-level inserts. Separately, my personal project uses dbt dimensions, facts and tests to create trustworthy analytical datasets.

projects.title: Retail Sales Lakehouse
projects.description: A personal batch lakehouse processing 500K+ records across six PostgreSQL entities, plus API ingestion. Airflow coordinates six parallel Bronze jobs and PySpark Silver transformations with window-based deduplication, schema enforcement, FX enrichment and row-level rejects. Transactional watermarks support incremental loads; batch-date partitioned Parquet and runtime parameters make processing repeatable and idempotent. Snowflake stages and COPY INTO feed dbt staging, dimensions, facts and analytical models, validated with unique, not-null and relationship tests.
